newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel bars Arab home repairs near Hebron settlers.
newsitem.headline: Israel bars Arab home repairs near Hebron settlers.

text.p: Israel stopped workmen from renovating Arab houses near Jewish enclaves in Hebron on Monday, which Palestinians said violated their redeployment deal.

Palestinians said Israeli police detained 11 men working in the old city of Hebron after military authorities delivered an order signed by West bank military commander Major General Uzi Dayan prohibiting the work. The army called it a security measure to protect Jewish settlers.
"The ink on the Hebron redeployment agreement has not dried yet and they are already violating the deal," Khaled al-Qawasmi, chief engineer for Hebron's Old City Renovations Committee told Reuters.
"We have permits from the Hebron municipality, which according to the agreement is responsible for civilian affairs in all of the city," he said.

Israel handed over 80 percent of Hebron to Palestinian self-rule 10 days ago under a redeployment deal but its troops continue to patrol the 20 percent of the city where some 400 Jewish settlers live or study among more than 20,000 Palestinians.
An Israeli army statement said Dayan issued the order as a security measure to protect the settlers.
Qawasmi said the order affects 38 apartments in 20 buildings, most of which are now under repair. He said about 120 apartments were being renovated throughout Hebron's Old City.
Many Hebron Palestinians, who had left homes in the old city after militant Jewish settlers moved into Hebron in 1979, have been trying to return to their houses.
"Many people left their homes because of settlers' harassment. Now in the time of peace they want to go back," Qawasmi said.
